title: Blind Channel Estimation and Equalization: Cumulants vs Autoencoder
content: This study addresses the problem of blind channel estimation and equalization in the context of OFDMA signals transmitted over Rayleigh multipath fading channels, modeled using BRAN-A, BRAN-B, and Proakis B profiles. Two distinct algorithmic paradigms are compared: a statistical method based on fourth-order cumulants (HOS) and a deep learning approach using autoencoders. Simulation results, conducted across a range of signal-to-noise ratios (SNR) and under noisy channel conditions, reveal the following: the fourth-order cumulant algorithm is characterized by its computational simplicity and analytical interpretability, delivering strong performance in stationary, low-noise environments. However, its performance significantly degrades under rapid channel variations or high noise levels. In contrast, the autoencoder-based approach demonstrates superior robustness and adaptability in complex, nonlinear, or time-varying scenarios. Its strength lies in its ability to implicitly learn and compensate for channel effects from raw data without requiring explicit modeling. This enhanced performance comes at the cost of increased computational complexity and reduced interpretability. In conclusion, while the cumulant-based method remains relevant in structured and stable environments, the autoencoder outperforms it in challenging channel conditions, offering a more powerful and flexible solution for blind equalization in modern communication systems.
